headlines.article_text: Bank earnings October 2026: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu watch now VIDEO 4:05 04:05 Bank earnings on deck this week: What to expect Squawk on the Street Four of the largest U.S. banks are reporting third-quarter results before the market opens on Tuesday: JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo are first out of the gates. Goldman Sachs and Citigroup are reporting later Tuesday morning, and Bank of America and Morgan Stanley will post earnings on Wednesday. The quarter was dominated by headlines around artificial intelligence, IPO uncertainty, high fuel prices and rising borrowing costs. All four reports on Tuesday are due by 8 a.m. ET, and executives from each of the banks will be addressing those topics and more during earnings calls between 8:30 a.m. and 11 a.m. ET. Here's what you need to know: JPM earnings are out WFC is out with its earnings What Wall Street is expecting from GS Analyst expectations for Citi Questions surround Wall Street's deal outlook Goldman's succession planning in the spotlight 5 Min Ago Shares of Wells Fargo are down slightly Wells Fargo stock is down just over 1% in premarket trading after the bank missed expectations on the top line but beat on the bottom line. The stock has declined roughly 10% this year. — Laya Neelakandan 9 Min Ago JPMorgan's third-quarter EPS misses the mark Jamie Dimon, chief executive officer of JPMorgan Chase & Co., during a Bloomberg Television interview on the sidelines of the JPMorgan Tech Stars Conference 2026 in London, UK, on Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. Jose Sarmento Matos | Bloomberg | Getty Images JPMorgan's results appear to be a rare miss for the largest U.S. bank by assets. The company put up third-quarter net income of $15.31 billion, or $5.57 per share. Excluding $658 million in net securities losses, EPS would've been higher at $5.75 per share, but that's still below the $5.90 estimate of analysts surveyed by LSEG. Before this report, JPMorgan had topped EPS estimates 16 of the past 20 quarters, per StreetAccount. The bank's shares are off about 3.5% in premarket trading. — Hugh Son 12 Min Ago Wells Fargo maintains guidance Wells Fargo said on Tuesday that it's maintaining its guidance for net interest income this year. It's also maintaining its guidance for non-interest expenses. – Laya Neelakandan 18 Min Ago Wells Fargo's net interest income came in slightly below expectations Analysts had been expecting Wells Fargo to report $12.66 billion in net interest income. The bank actually reported $12.52 billion on Tuesday. It also said it saw a $1.03 billion provision for credit losses, just under StreetAccount expectations of $1.14 billion. – Laya Neelakandan 21 Min Ago Wells Fargo reports strength across segment revenues Wells Fargo said wealth and investment management revenue grew 12% compared with the year-ago period. It also saw consumer banking and lending grow 5%, corporate and investment banking grow 3% and commercial banking rise by 6%. It also said it opened more than 660,000 new credit card accounts in the quarter. — Laya Neelakandan 23 Min Ago Wells Fargo says consumer remains resilient Charles Scharf, chief executive officer of Wells Fargo & Co., during a Bloomberg Television interview in New York, US, on Wednesday, July 22, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Wells Fargo reported that despite macroeconomic pressures and overall uncertainty, consumers remain resilient. "Consumers are spending more, loan delinquencies are low, and deposit and investment balances have grown," CEO Scharf said in a statement. "While higher interest rates, higher oil prices and persistent inflation create risks to the economy, strong positive forces such as the investment in AI infrastructure, high employment levels and consistent wage growth continue to outweigh the risks." — Laya Neelakandan 24 Min Ago JPMorgan earnings are out — here are the numbers watch now VIDEO 1:55 01:55 JPMorgan misses on top and bottom lines in Q3 Squawk Box Here's what JPMorgan reported compared with analysts' consensus estimates, according to LSEG: Earnings per share: $5.57, may not compare with $5.90 per share expected Revenue: $50.91 billion vs. $51.22 billion expected — Sara Salinas 30 Min Ago Wells Fargo earnings are out — here are the numbers watch now VIDEO 1:45 01:45 Wells Fargo reports mixed Q3 results Squawk Box Here's what Wells Fargo reported compared with analysts' consensus estimates, according to LSEG: Earnings per share: $1.87 vs. $1.85 per share expected Revenue: $21.87 billion vs. $22.3 billion expected — Sara Salinas 45 Min Ago The Muse effect: Do banks face disruption risk from AI agents? Mark Zuckerberg, CEO of the Facebook parent company Meta, takes the stage at the Meta Connect developer conference. Andrej Sokolow | Picture Alliance | Getty Images One likely topic for today's analyst calls will be around whether banks aren't just the beneficiary of AI, but at risk from it. Specifically, AI agents like Meta's Muse could make it easier for customers to move money from accounts that pay almost nothing to accounts with higher yields. Last month, Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok even outlined a possible bank run scenario caused by AI. "If every household used AI agents to optimize the return on their cash balances, banks could lose a large share of the cheap deposits they rely on to make loans," Slok wrote. That would "be a problem for the entire financial system." Some banks faced higher deposit costs last quarter, but that's amid the backdrop of surging Treasury yields, according to StreetAccount. Bank stocks were hit by concerns over AI agents last month, just as shares of Meta were rising as its Muse app topped the app download charts. But over the longer term, banks will develop their own agent interfaces, insulating them from the threat, Bank of America analyst Ebrahim Poonawala said in an Oct. 4 note. "Investors continue to inquire about the potential for agentic AI to disrupt banking deposits, fees, margins and customer acquisition," Poonawala wrote. "While the timing and magnitude remain uncertain, one implication is becoming clearer: banks may increasingly need to build for the agent, not just the customer." — Hugh Son 1 Hour Ago Oura's shelved IPO raises questions about Wall Street's deal outlook Tom Hale, chief executive officer of Oura Health Oy, wears an Oura Ring during an interview in San Francisco, California, US, on Friday, June 14, 2024. Those are the questions analysts will have for Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase after a string of high-profile IPOs were put on hold in recent months, including the listing of smart ring maker Oura , which cited uncertain market conditions as its reason for delay. Global investment banking revenue in the third quarter fell 6.6% from a year earlier to $27.2 billion, thanks to declines in closed mergers and debt issuance, according to Dealogic data. But the slowdown is far from uniform across Wall Street. Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan warned in September that third-quarter investment banking fees were headed for a decline of more than 10%, while trading revenue will be roughly flat. headlines.article_text: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article JNJ Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Johnson & Johnson offices in Irvine, California, on Friday, Oct. 10, 2025. Kyle Grillot | Bloomberg | Getty Images Johnson & Johnson ⁠reported a slightly higher-than-expected profit on Tuesday, driven by strong sales of immune disease treatment Tremfya, but geopolitical ​issues, including the Middle ​East conflict, were a drag ​on its medical-devices business. The company posted third-quarter revenue of $25.4 billion, above analysts' average estimate of $25.28 billion, according to LSEG data. Adjusted earnings of $2.59 per share also topped ⁠Wall Street ‌expectations of $2.54. Pharmaceutical sales jumped 7.7% in the quarter ⁠to $16.76 billion. Medical technology division sales rose only 2.5% to $8.6 billion overall. Outside the U.S., the division's sales were essentially flat. J&J Chief Financial Officer Joe Wolk said in an interview that the Mideast conflict, austerity measures in Europe, and pricing in China continued to weigh on international results, "but maybe in a little bit more pronounced way." He said ​the Mideast conflict, which has driven up fuel costs at home and abroad, has not yet affected the company's costs but has hurt sales in the region. "These are countries that still value and actually ⁠want premium healthcare systems, think Kuwait, UAE, Saudi Arabia. They pride themselves on having solid healthcare, ‌very good healthcare," Wolk said. "But their budgets now are ‌being resourced and allocated towards defense." Sales at its Abiomed heart pump business also remained slow after a UK study earlier this year raised questions about using Impella pumps during certain high-risk coronary procedures. Tremfya sales rose 68% to $2.4 billion, beating analyst estimates of about $2.19 billion, while Stelara sales, which face generic competition, fell 54% to $716 million, still well above Wall Street expectations of $591 million. Tremfya has increasingly replaced lost Stelara revenue following recent approvals in inflammatory ​bowel diseases. Sales of blood cancer treatment ‌Darzalex rose about 16% to $4.24 billion, short of analyst expectations of $4.4 billion. The company raised its full-year sales forecast to about $101.2 billion at the midpoint, from $101.1 billion previously. It increased its adjusted earnings forecast range with a new midpoint of $11.10 per share, up from $11.04. J&J ​shares closed at $263.73 on Monday. They ‌have risen 27% this year, outperforming both the broader market and most healthcare peers. headlines.title: UnitedHealth Group tops estimates, hikes profit outlook as insurer manages high medical costs
headlines.summary: UnitedHealth Group said it expects 2026 adjusted earnings of at least $20.50 per share, up from a previous outlook of $19.50 to $20.00 per share.
headlines.article_text: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points UnitedHealth Group posted third-quarter earnings that blew past estimates and raised its full-year profit outlook. The nation's largest private insurer continues to manage high medical costs and is seeing investments in value-based care and artificial intelligence take hold, CFO Wayne DeVeydt said in an interview. The company said it expects fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of at least $20.50 per share, up from a previous outlook of $19.50 to $20 per share. In this article UNH Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT UnitedHealth Group signage on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange on April 21, 2025. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images UnitedHealth Group on Tuesday posted third-quarter earnings that blew past estimates and raised its full-year profit outlook, as the company continues to manage high medical costs and sees investments in value-based care and artificial intelligence take hold. The nation's largest private insurer said it expects fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of at least $20.50 per share, up from a previous outlook of $19.50 to $20 per share. The healthcare giant's turnaround plan is gaining momentum after three consecutive strong quarters this year. UnitedHealth is working to stabilize margins by shrinking membership, exiting unprofitable contracts and ramping up investments in artificial intelligence and value-based care, which tie doctor and facility compensation to patient health outcomes, quality of care and cost effectiveness rather than the volume of medical services provided. "You'll see in the quarter that we continue to execute not only on the financial aspects of our business, but really doing them with a simpler approach and an approach that's really focused on investing heavily in value-based care," CFO Wayne DeVeydt said in an interview. Shares of the company rose about 3% in premarket trading. Here's what the company reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $4.69 adjusted vs. $4.14 expected Revenue: $112.69 billion vs. $111.40 billion expected The company posted third-quarter net income of $4.11 billion, or $4.56 per share, compared with $2.35 billion, or $2.59 per share, in the same period a year ago. Excluding items like business divestitures, restructuring and the expected reduction of reserves for unprofitable contracts, UnitedHealth earned $4.69 per share. Revenue fell to $112.69 billion from $113.16 billion in the prior-year quarter. The company's insurer, UnitedHealthcare, and its Optum healthcare unit both topped analysts' operating earnings estimates for the quarter, according to StreetAccount. Managing high costs Notably, UnitedHealth's medical cost ratio — a measure of total medical expenses paid relative to premiums collected — came in at 88.4% for the third quarter. Analysts were expecting a ratio of 89.9% for the quarter, according to StreetAccount. A lower ratio typically indicates that the company collected more in premiums than it paid out in benefits, resulting in higher profitability. Still, DeVeydt told CNBC that medical costs in the quarter "continue to be elevated versus historical norms" – an issue that has plagued insurers, particularly those operating privately run Medicare Advantage plans, for more than two years. "I think it's something we should keep an eye on. I think you'll see that our medical care ratio has improved quite a bit, but I don't want that to be misleading in terms of [medical cost trends]," DeVeydt said. He said the independent dispute resolution (IDR) process under the No Surprises Act is adding at least 100 basis points, or 1 percentage point, to total medical costs. That federal law, which took effect in 2022, aims to protect consumers from unexpected medical bills The IDR process allows providers and insurers to resolve disputes over out-of-network payments. DeVeydt said those changes are driving up the company's claims costs, which can ultimately be passed on to consumers through higher premiums. DeVeydt added that costs for inpatient services and pharmacy, particularly costly specialty pharmacy drugs for cancer and rare diseases, remain elevated. Still, he highlighted the company's value-based care efforts, which are helping control medical costs by steering patients toward the right providers and emphasizing preventive care, DeVeydt added. He said acute hospital admissions among UnitedHealth members fell 15% year over year through the third quarter, while home health admissions rose 10%, suggesting more patients are receiving care in lower-cost settings. "You're finding more members are actually getting into a lower-cost care environment, but more importantly, they're getting into the care environment they actually want to be in," he told CNBC. "So we think we're really balancing both the quality and the cost." UnitedHealth is also rolling out AI-powered ambient listening tools to reduce physicians' administrative burden and free up time for patient visits. Appointment scheduling done by patients rather than with the assistance of a provider increased 27% year over year, DeVeydt said. He expects those initiatives to have a compounding effect on medical cost management through the fourth quarter and into 2027 as the programs expand. The article said that Guilfoyle told people who were the targets of her effort that "they should deal with a Greek construction firm called Aktor Group, a newcomer to the gas business that had teamed up with a Greek state-backed energy company to bring in liquefied natural gas from the U.S." The article detailed how Guilfoyle had traveled frequently with a top lobbyist for Aktor named Christos Marafatsos, who has been "joining her for meetings at her ambassadorial residence and with government officials in countries around the region—a highly unusual move for a private citizen." On Oct. 7, the Journal published an article detailing how Guilfoyle allegedly asked a Trump donor named Eric Deters in July 2025 to pay $100,000 for what she said was an American Express bill before her upcoming Senate confirmation hearing for the ambassadorship. A lawyer for Guilfoyle told the newspaper that Deters owed her a balance for "traveling to and supporting" events where she was hired to speak. On Saturday, the Journal published another article that said during the January 2026 World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, she had "boasted ... about her close ties to two Greek tycoons and said they were bankrolling her high-rolling trips around the world." In a statement on Sunday, Guilfoyle's lawyers "denied she had done anything wrong and claimed that the money she was seeking from the Trump donor was payment for services — public appearances and speaking engagements that predate her ambassadorial nomination — that had not been paid," The Associated Press reported. headlines.article_text: SpaceX agrees to testify to NYC Council about AI safety Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points SpaceX has agreed to testify before the New York City Council as part of an investigation into artificial intelligence safety risks. The city council subpoenaed SpaceX CEO Elon Musk ordering that he or another representative testify at a hearing last week. SpaceX skipped that hearing, while representatives from Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Google all testified. In this article SPCX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT SpaceX CEO Elon Musk attends a meeting with US President Donald Trump and technology executives about artificial intelligence in the East Room of the White House in Washington, DC, on Sept. 29, 2026. Kent Nishimura | AFP | Getty Images SpaceX has agreed to testify before the New York City Council this week as part of a legislative investigation concerning artificial intelligence safety risks, the council announced on Tuesday. The council said in a press release that the hearing will take place on Friday at 10 a.m. ET in front of its tech committee. Julie Menin, council speaker, and Nwamaka Ejebe, general counsel, issued a subpoena to Elon Musk and SpaceX's AI unit on Sept. 28, compelling testimony for a hearing that took place last week. Representatives from Anthropic , OpenAI , Google and Meta all testified at the hearing on Oct. 5, but SpaceX did not appear. Menin said in Tuesday's statement that SpaceX agreed two days later to testify after the council said it intended to have its subpoena enforced by a judge. "Last Monday, we held a major, hours-long hearing with whistleblowers, the world's largest tech companies, and the nation's foremost experts in AI," Menin said in Tuesday's release. "Conspicuously absent was SpaceXAI, which is unacceptable." Musk folded his AI venture, xAI, into SpaceX in February, creating a conglomerate that includes its Grok models, which are used by some federal agencies, including the Pentagon . SpaceX went public in June and is now valued at over $2 trillion. In August, SpaceX also completed a $60 billion acquisition of AI coding startup Cursor. SpaceX competes with Anthropic and OpenAI in the AI market, though Grok trails far behind models from top rivals. The NYC council opened its investigation following a month of intense debate surrounding the risks posed by advanced AI models. In its original letter ordering testimony from Musk or another SpaceX leader, the council said its investigation would help, "assess whether fast-emerging risks to public safety, cybersecurity, economic stability, privacy, consumers and businesses warrant immediate legislative action to protect New Yorkers." SpaceX's "failure to comply" with the subpoena, the council warned, could subject the company to penalties or other punishment under New York City laws and regulations. Carmen De La Rosa, chair of the tech committee, told CNBC in a statement that the council expects answers from SpaceX. "With the proliferation of Elon Musk's technology at the federal level, it is even more important they come to the discussion with robust context about data privacy, safeguards, and whistleblower protections," she said. Lawsuits are piling up against SpaceX after Grok's image generator enabled mass production and distribution of deepfake porn based on images of real people who did consent. SpaceX didn't respond to a request for comment. — CNBC's Ashley Capoot contributed reporting. headlines.summary: Technology stocks tumbled Tuesday as a sell-off in U.S. semiconductor shares spilled into Asian and European markets.
headlines.article_text: Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, ASML shares: tech stocks fall Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Technology stocks tumbled Tuesday as a sell-off in U.S. semiconductor shares spilled into Asian and European markets. China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, reported progress on a new chip structure, intensifying chip competition. Intel and Broadcom CEOs have warned that access to capital could emerge as a major headwind to the artificial intelligence boom. In this article 9984.T-JP ASML STM IFX-DE SKHY Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Samuel Boivin | Nurphoto | Getty Images Technology stocks fell Tuesday, extending a sell-off sparked by worries over artificial intelligence financing and intensifying competition. Memory chip giant Micron was down around 3% in U.S. premarket trading, with other names like Broadcom under pressure. Other memory-related stocks such as SanDisk , Seagate and Western Digital were all around 3% lower. The slide, which follows declines on Wall Street on Monday, comes as investors assessed intensifying competition from China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT . Micron shares year-to-date. Over the weekend , CXMT announced significant progress in developing a new chip architecture, designed to increase memory density by packing more data into a smaller space. CXMT is China's leading rival to the likes of Micron and South Korean heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics. Analysts broadly see CXMT as trailing the U.S. and South Korean memory leaders, which means any advancement from the Chinese firm could add more competition to the market leaders. "Investors are jittery and looking for excuses to take profit on AI-related stocks that have outperformed this year, especially memory stocks," said UBP's senior equity advisor Vey-Sern Ling. "In reality, while the Chinese memory makers can potentially become a threat to global demand-supply balance over time, in the short run they continue to face technology hurdles, especially for more advanced memory like HBM," Ling told CNBC via email. CXMT shares closed 2.8% lower in Shanghai. Global tech stocks slump Adding fuel to the sell-off was a post by Tesla and SpaceX boss Elon Musk, who said China has the ability to scale production once it figures out how to manufacture something. "When China figures out how to manufacture a product, their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined," Musk said on Monday. European chip stocks also sank in early morning trade, with semiconductor equipment maker ASML down 3.3%, and STMicroelectronics and German chip maker Infineon both down 5%. Dutch firms BE Semiconductor and ASM International were both around 4% lower at the open. Shares of South Korean chip giant SK Hynix, a leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory chips used in artificial intelligence applications, plunged more than 10%, while rival Samsung Electronics shed 7.4% — both hitting their lowest levels since August. SK Hynix's U.S.-listed stock was down around 5% in premarket trading. watch now VIDEO 4:30 04:30 Tech shakedown spreads as U.S. heavyweights face fresh selling Squawk Box Europe In Japan, shares of tech-focused investment giant SoftBank Group sank 8.5%. The group, which has significant exposure to the global AI industry through its huge investment in OpenAI, led a broader retreat in Japanese semiconductor and electronics shares. Tokyo Electron , a major supplier of chipmaking equipment, dropped 7.2%, while Advantest , which makes semiconductor testing equipment, declined 2.9%. Other Japanese technology stocks also came under pressure. Lasertec fell over 5%, Disco lost 4.7% and Renesas Electronics shed 5.9%. The declines followed a weak session for technology stocks on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.44% on Monday. U.S. memory chipmaker Micron Technology slid 3.9% as 'Vulnerable' AI sentiment? Phillip Wool, chief market strategist at Rayliant Global Advisors, said CXMT's breakthrough marked a significant milestone for Chinese chipmakers , demonstrating their ability to overcome technology restrictions and potentially challenge established players sooner than expected. But he cautioned that the market reaction appeared disproportionate to the immediate competitive threat, given that CXMT has yet to demonstrate large-scale production and continues to lag Samsung and SK Hynix in market share. "More importantly, we're not even talking about HBM here, and the Korean chipmakers are still unquestionably dominating that space, with very little threat at all from the likes of CXMT or anyone else for the foreseeable future," Wool said. He said the sharp sell-off reflected broader anxiety over the AI trade rather than a fundamental shift in the competitive landscape. "I read that more as a sign of how vulnerable AI sentiment is at this moment," Wool said, warning that volatility could persist as investors reassess chip demand and how long semiconductor manufacturers can sustain their pricing power. The chief executives of Intel and Broadcom have warned that access to capital could emerge as a major headwind to the AI boom, even as demand for computing infrastructure continues to outstrip supply. Investors are also looking ahead to a busy week of corporate earnings and U.S. inflation data, which could provide fresh clues on the outlook for interest rates that often have an inverse correlation with growth stocks.
